nodes.name: Amorphization reaction
nodes.procedure: Pt1/TiO2 as source to react with NaBH4 at 400°C for 4 h, and after that the amorphous TiB_xO_y supported single Pt atom was obtained.
nodes.source_text: Chen et al. applied Pt1/TiO2 as source to react with NaBH4 at 400°C for 4 h , and after that the amorphous TiB_xO_y supported single Pt atom was obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Ru K-edge XANES of Ru1/Pt3Cu shows little change in coordination environment at 1.86 V vs RHE, indicating excellent OER stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the single Ru atom formed a stable coordination environment with little changes in Ru K-edge, by alloying with Pt under a high OER applied voltage of 1.86 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), implying materials' excellent OER stability (Figure 3f)

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Pt L3-edge XANES of Ru1/Pt3Cu shows obvious increase in intensity with applied voltage, suggesting increased d-band center and electron transfer from Pt to Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: an obvious increase of Pt L3 edge intensity was detected with the increase of applied voltages (Figure 3g), which suggested an increased d-band center for Pt in Pt3Cu alloys and the electrons transfer from Pt to single Ru atoms

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-IR of Ru1/Pt3Cu shows disappearance of OOHad peak (1212 cm⁻¹) during OER, indicating adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) not LOER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ attenuated total reflection infrared spectra (ATR-IR) also demonstrated the disappeared OOHad (1212 cm⁻¹) on Ru1/Pt3Cu during OER, which suggested the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) for OER not the LOER

nodes.characterization_summary: High-magnification STEM shows single Ir atoms coordinated with Ir-O on NiO host.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-magnification scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) of Ir1/NiO

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS Ir L3-edge of Ir1/MnO2 shows shorter Ir-O bond (1.877 Å) vs IrO2 (1.982 Å), indicating strong Ir-O covalency (Figure 4c).
nodes.evidence_snippet: 5d orbital of single Ir atom overlapped with 2p orbital of O from γMnO2 in Ir1/MnO2 at Fermi level... Such strong Ir-O covalency was revealed by a shorter length of Ir-O bond (1.877 Å) compared to the one (1.982 Å) in IrO2 (Figure 4c)

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Ir L3-edge XANES of Ir0.1/Ni9Fe shows valence state increase from ~+4 at OCV to +5.3 under OER voltage (Figure 5a,b).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In OER process, the valence state of Ir increased from near +4 under open circuit voltage (OCV) to +5.3 under reaction voltage... Experimental Ir L3 edge XANES spectra at OCV and different potentials (Figure 5a)

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM shows Ir atoms as bright spots dispersed on amorphous (oxy)hydroxide surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM image of Ir1/NiFeO. Ir atoms appeared as bright spots (highlighted by the white circles) and were dispersed on the amorphous surface

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge FT-EXAFS of Ir1/NiFeP shows dominant Ir-O peak at 1.78 Å; Ir coordinated by 4 O ligands + 2 O from OH/H2O (Figure 6d).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-EXAFS spectra showed a dominant peak at 1.78Å corresponding to the Ir-O scattering feature, and that one Ir atom was coordinated with four O atoms from oxygen ligands and two O atoms from adsorbed hydroxyl or water group (Figure 6d)

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Ni/Fe K-edge FT-EXAFS of Ir1/NiFeP shows stable Ir/Fe environment but Ni valence increase and Ni-O bond shrinkage during OER (Figure 6f,g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ir and Fe atoms in superficial Ir1/NiFeO exhibited a stable chemical environment during OER, while an increased valence state of Ni was clearly observed in situ EXAFS spectra... Such shrinkage further fixed the isolated Ir atoms (Figure 6f,g)
